newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Euro bourses rise, FTSE and DAX hit records.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Euro bourses rise, FTSE and DAX hit records.

text.p: European bourses rose sharply on Thursday, with British and German shares climbing to record highs.

Sterling remained strong but slipped off its high after remarks from UK Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown. He said exporters should benefit from the rebalancing of monetary and fiscal policy in his budget on Wednesday but that he remained unhappy with sterling's strength.
"Of course, I want a stable and competitive pound," Brown said. "I wanted to mitigate the pressures on exporters. Nobody can be happy about an 18-percent rise in the pound in current circumstances."
Though prospects for a lower currency are normally supportive for stocks in a low-inflation environment, traders said Thursday's rise in London's FTSE-100 index owed little to his comments.
The FTSE made the most stunning gains among European bourses in the morning, overcoming steep opening losses to soar more than 100 points to a record high by late morning.
The rise came despite expectations of at least a couple of UK interest rate rises by year-end.

"The average fund manager is not as gloomy as the average economist," said Darren Winder, SBC Warburg economist. "Upward revisions in interest rate forecasts are not seen as a big negative, with the feeling that the more they rise now, the less damage we'll see longer term."
Banks and utility shares led the FTSE's rally. Banks rose on earnings considerations and takeover prospects, ignoring the forecasts of higher UK rates.
But the pound's strength was too much for exporters to shrug off. Exporters' shares plunged, worried that the strong currency would eat away earnings.
Germany's DAX index also scored a record high early in line with Wall Street's sharp gains overnight after the Federal Reserve left U.S. rates unchanged, as expected.
The blue-chip Dow Jones Industrial Average surged in the final hour of trading to close up 73 points at 7,795.

Traders were looking for the DAX to break the key psychological level at 4,000 soon. But DAX gains could be limited in the afternoon, depending on the Dow's reaction to key U.S. monthly jobs and inflation data due at 1230 GMT.
A Reuters survey forecast June non-farm payrolls to gain 220,000 after May's 138,000 rise. Average hourly wages were seen jumping 0.4 percent.
Traders will be looking for soft U.S. data to confirm the Fed's steady rate stance on Wednesday.
Paris' CAC-40 index was also buoyed by the Dow's gains and the firm U.S. dollar.

LVMH's 3.25-percent jump also helped the CAC-40. LVMH gained after Britain's Guinness and Grand Met said they were open to proposals to bring LVMH's drinks business into their planned merger. At 1130 GMT, LVMH shares were up 55 at 1,635 French francs.
Thomson-CSF also rose about 2.5 percent on hopes its privatisation may go ahead. At 1130 GMT, Thomson was up four at 160.50 francs.
In currency markets, the dollar held in narrow ranges above 114 yen and 1.75 marks, just below a 40-month high, in early trading as the market awaited the U.S. data.
"It will be very quiet...waiting for the minutes of the last Fed meeting and the unemployment figures, which could give the market a bit of a lift," said Peter Wood, Bank of Boston dealer.
After U.S. data are released, traders said dollar trading could be quiet as dealing winds down before the long Fourth of July weekend. U.S. markets are closed on Friday.
CURRENCIES AT 1125 GMT
The dollar was at 114.30 yen and 1.7543 marks compared with 114.44 and 1.7515 in late Europe on Wednesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1125 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 42.6 points at 4,794.00.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was up 12.36 at 2,921.81.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was up 36.45 at 3,891.21.
PRECIOUS METALS
London gold was fixed at $332.30 an ounce, up from $332.35 at Wednesday's close. Silver opened unchanged at $4.66.
